endorsements.quote: To mitigate this, data sets must be large enough, and split into separate training/validation and testing sets, ensuring that test data remain completely unseen during model development, including during parameter tuning.

High inter‐rater variability such as in EEG review underscores the importance of using multiple expert raters who are ideally blinded to study groups or outcomes, as well as using standardized definition criteria 35 and annotation instruments.

Second, effect sizes and measures of dispersion, such as confidence intervals, should be reported to contextualize model reliability, and feature importance analyses can help interpret model explainability.
Whenever possible, preprocessing code should be made publicly available to enable independent verification and replication.
Compare it with current existing similar solutions. Simpler methods are preferred if performance is comparable.
Describe all data sources used for model training and testing, including type, representativeness, and rationale.
Ensure transparency and reproducibility by sharing code, models, and documentation.

unlisted_practices: Address or correct for class imbalance in AI training and test data.
Perform and report sample size estimation or power calculation, or justify a small sample size.
Address multiple comparisons and false discovery rate in statistical analyses.
Describe and justify handling of missing or poor-quality data, including imputation or exclusion procedures.
Report participant flow, follow-up, and loss to follow-up.
Report and address confounding in AI studies.
Report acceptability, usability, and safety of the technology among relevant stakeholders, including adherence and adverse events.
Describe how patients, clinicians, and caregivers were involved in technology and AI design.
Avoid commercial bias and interpret results fairly when reporting AI study results.
Use clinically relevant performance metrics appropriate to the use case, not accuracy alone in imbalanced data.
Justify the choice of AI or new technology and describe how it adds to the existing clinical workflow.
Consider whether models are fair and at risk of perpetuating biases in the data.
Describe technology integration into clinical workflow, including technical requirements, user expertise, and limitations, and the target population.
Use an appropriate clinical reference standard for direct and fair comparison with the AI solution.
Use a control group or intervention to isolate the effect of the new technology.
Use consistent, accepted terminology and plain language adapted to the target audience.

screen.reason: The paper provides reporting guidelines and recommendations for authors and peer reviewers regarding AI and neurotechnology studies in epilepsy, based on an analysis of peer-review comments.
